body_markdown:
Apple doesn't replace an entire product line lightly. The iPhone Air isn't a variant of the iPhone 17 — it's a brand-new category, replacing the Plus model entirely, built around a single, deliberate idea: how thin and light can a genuinely capable iPhone actually be.

## What Apple Actually Said at the Keynote

Apple's senior vice president of Hardware Engineering, John Ternus, introduced the Air by framing it as something you have to physically hold to understand: an iPhone so thin and light that it feels almost implausible while still delivering "pro performance" and "great all-day battery life." He described it as "a brand-new member of the iPhone family," not an evolution of an existing model.

The headline number is 5.6mm thick — thinner than any iPhone Apple has ever shipped. To hit that number, Apple made real trade-offs: the iPhone Air is eSIM-only (no physical SIM tray at all), and it ships with a single 48MP rear camera rather than the multi-lens system on the Pro line. What it keeps is a 6.5–6.6-inch Super Retina XDR display with 120Hz ProMotion, the same A19 Pro chip family used in the Pro line, and Center Stage front camera.

## Colors and Finishes

The iPhone Air's four colors were designed specifically to suit its design-forward, minimalist identity:

- **Sky Blue** — a soft, light finish that's become one of the most popular Air colors since launch.
- **Cloud White** — a clean, versatile classic.
- **Light Gold** — an elegant, understated warm tone. Apple highlighted the new polished titanium finish on the Air as having "an elegant mirrored finish."
- **Space Black** — the one darker option, for anyone who wants the Air's thin profile without a lighter color statement.

## Why This Device Actually Matters

- **5.6mm profile, sub-165g weight** — genuinely different in the hand from any other current iPhone; this isn't a marginal size reduction.
- **Titanium frame** — despite the thinness, Apple built the Air to be, in its own words, "more durable than any previous iPhone."
- **Same core silicon as the Pro line** — you're not getting a downgraded chip just because the body is thinner.
- **eSIM only** — a genuine trade-off worth knowing before you buy: there is no physical SIM slot, so you'll need a carrier that supports eSIM activation (Safaricom and Airtel both do in Kenya).
- **Single-camera system** — the Air trades multi-lens versatility for its thin profile; if zoom range matters most to you, the standard iPhone 17 or Pro line is the better fit.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What is the iPhone Air price in Kenya?**
Brand new iPhone Air prices at Affordable Gadgets KE range from KSh 124,500 to KSh 128,500 depending on color and warranty option.

**What colors does the iPhone Air come in?**
Four finishes: Sky Blue, Cloud White, Light Gold, and Space Black.

**Does the iPhone Air have a physical SIM slot?**
No — the iPhone Air is eSIM only. Both Safaricom and Airtel support eSIM activation in Kenya.

**How thin is the iPhone Air really?**
5.6mm — the thinnest iPhone Apple has ever made, noticeably slimmer than the standard iPhone 17 or Pro models.

**Does the iPhone Air have the same camera as the iPhone 17 Pro?**
No — the Air has a single 48MP rear camera rather than the Pro's multi-lens system, which is part of how Apple achieved the thin profile.

**Who is the iPhone Air actually built for?**
Anyone who prioritizes how the phone feels in hand and pocket over having the longest zoom range or a physical SIM slot — it's a design-first phone rather than a spec-maximizing one.

## The Bottom Line

The iPhone Air is Apple's clearest statement yet that not every iPhone needs to chase the most cameras or the biggest battery. If you want the thinnest, lightest iPhone ever made, with genuine flagship performance underneath, and you're comfortable going eSIM-only, this is a phone built specifically around that trade-off — and it delivers on it.
